Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

we are planning a refresh of the Lantern Room Reading Club website, and i need the new pages to make the club easier to understand for people who have not attended before. Please keep the existing name, the Wednesday meeting schedule, and the monthly book selection as they are. The club meets in the back room of Alder Street Library, and meetings run from 6:30 to 8:00 p.m. The site should say that newcomers can attend one meeting before joining, but they should not have to make an account just to read the public pages. We want the tone to feel friendly, not like a library policy notice. One member described the current homepage as “a door with no handle,” which is a useful way to explain why the main links need to be easier to find.

The homepage needs a short explanation of how the club works, a link to the current book, the date of the next meeting, and a clear way to ask a question. Please do not put the full book discussion guide on the homepage; that belongs on the page for the current selection. The meeting date should come from the event listing, rather than being typed separately in two places, because we have had the dates disagree before. If no future meeting has been entered, show “Next meeting to be announced” instead of leaving an empty date area. We also need a small note that the library is closed on federal holidays, since a meeting can be moved when one falls on Wednesday. The note should not say that every Wednesday meeting is canceled on a holiday; the coordinator confirms the date first.

For the current book page, show the title, author, publisher, the month it is being discussed, and the discussion guide as a downloadable PDF. Our volunteer who prepares the guide prefers to upload it herself, so please make that a simple upload field in the club admin area. The site should not create a guide automatically if the PDF is missing. In that case, leave the guide link off the public page, and show the admin a reminder that the file still needs to be added. We would like the public page to include a brief description, but not a review or a star rating. Members sometimes disagree about a book, and a rating would look like an official club opinion. One of the organizers said, “A lively discussion is not the same thing as a unanimous recommendation.”

Members can make an account using an email address and a password. Please include an optional display name, which can be different from the name on the account, and let members change it later. The account page should have a saved shelf for books they want to read and a list of books they have already discussed with the club. These lists are private; they should not be visible to other members or included in public search results. A member may also choose to receive meeting reminders by email, but the choice should start turned off. Do not treat an account email as permission to send general announcements. General announcements need a separate, unchecked opt-in on the account page, with a short explanation of what kinds of messages that covers.

Please make the membership renewal rule visible before a member pays. If a renewal is recorded before the current membership expires, keep the member’s saved shelf and discussion history available without interruption. If renewal has not been recorded by the expiration date, mark the membership as lapsed and hide the saved shelf and history from the member’s account screen. Keep the account and its lists for 30 days after expiration so the member can export them if they return. After that 30-day period, delete the saved shelf and discussion history, but do not delete the account’s email address or password record automatically. The membership coordinator handles account removal separately. The renewal notice should explain these two outcomes in plain language, rather than suggesting that a late renewal will restore the lists after they have been deleted.

The event page should show upcoming meetings and any book-club events that are open to guests. Each listing needs a date, start and end time, location, and a short description. For events that have limited seats, members may register on the site. Please display the number of available seats, but do not show the names of people who registered. When the last seat is taken, close registration and offer a waitlist instead. If an event is marked as waitlisted, do not show seats as available; send a member a notification only if a spot opens and the member is next in line. The event coordinator needs to be able to change the event status from open to waitlisted or canceled, and the public page should reflect that status without delay.

The admin area needs to stay manageable for volunteers who only work on the site once or twice a month. Please make roles for coordinator, book-page editor, and event editor. A book-page editor should be able to change book details and upload a discussion guide, but not edit member accounts or event registrations. An event editor should be able to update listings and registration status, but not change the selected book. The coordinator can do both and can add or remove the other volunteer roles. For the first version, please keep the existing mailing list outside the website; do not import its addresses or send messages from the site. We may decide about a mailing-list connection later, but it is not part of this request.

1. Before launch, please check the following page behavior:
   - On a phone, the main navigation should fit without requiring horizontal scrolling.
   - Links to the current book and the next meeting should remain visible near the top of the homepage.
   - A missing discussion-guide PDF should remove the public download link and leave the admin reminder in place.
   - A canceled event should still appear in the event list with its status clearly shown, but registration should be closed.
   - A member’s private lists should not appear when someone visits a public book or event page.
   - The contact form should ask for an email address and question, and should show a confirmation after submission without publishing the message.

The website should work with a keyboard as well as a mouse, and the text should remain readable when enlarged. Please use clear labels for buttons and form fields, especially on the registration and account pages. We need a way to report a page problem that does not require signing in, so put the contact link in the footer on every page. If that form is unavailable, show the club’s existing contact email, lanternroom.club@example.org, rather than a blank form area. Keep the wording about the library’s location and accessibility exactly limited to the information supplied by the club; we do not yet have confirmation about step-free access.
